- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in the early part of the forecast horizon (first 5–10 days).
- After a price spike, model tends to overshoot and then gradually correct — but often lags the true mean reversion.
- Model underestimates prices in the final 5–10 days of the forecast, particularly when true prices show downward momentum.
- When history shows strong upward momentum, model fails to capture the full extent of the trend, underestimating peak values.
- Model exhibits persistent bias toward higher values, suggesting calibration needs for downward volatility or mean reversion weighting.
- In cases of sharp price drops, model fails to anticipate the drop, often forecasting a plateau or slight recovery instead.
- Model tends to smooth out volatility, underreacting to short-term price reversals or sudden policy-driven shifts.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts are prone to overconfidence in early days and underconfidence in late days — consider weighting recent history more heavily for the final 10 days.
